title: This is the parameter network
text: Every open fit is a large blue disc, and every parameter in it is a small disc joined to it by a thin grey line. The colour of a parameter says what it is doing: purple is free, green follows another parameter, grey is fixed. The key is in the top-left corner.

title: Show the fixed parameters too
text: A fixed parameter is not estimated, but it can still be linked — and it is hidden until you ask for it. Tick this to see the whole model.

title: Link two parameters by dragging
text: Drag from one parameter onto another. The one you dragged from becomes the follower: it stops being estimated and takes the other's value, and the arrow you drew stays, pointing at the master. That is what makes a fit global — two datasets sharing one lifetime.

title: …or by selecting and pressing Link
text: Click one parameter (it is the master), click a second, then press Link: the second follows the first. It works when the two nodes are far apart.

title: Edit what you selected
text: The Selection panel lists each selected parameter with the fit it belongs to — which matters, because two fits of the same model name their parameters identically — and its role: master, follower, fixed or free. Double-click a value to change it; a follower's value is its master's and cannot be typed.

title: Break a link
text: Select the follower and press Unlink, or break the arrow in the network. Tick ‘all’ first to clear every link in every fit at once.

title: See the fit as a factor graph
text: Switch Show to ‘Factor graph’. Each dataset becomes a square — its likelihood — joined to the variables it depends on, links resolved: a lifetime two datasets share is one gold variable joined to both squares. The status line counts the shared variables and the independent blocks: two blocks mean two fits that only look global.

title: When the network gets crowded
text: Change the Layout to move the nodes around, raise Spread to push them apart, then use the wheel to zoom and drag the background with the middle button to pan. Fit view puts everything back in the panel. Connect base joins the fits and plugin groups to each other, so you can see what is available to link against.

title: Keeping up with the fits
text: The network follows the fits by itself — changes are coalesced, and the layout only re-runs when the shape actually changed, so a running fit costs nothing here. Untick ‘auto’ to take that over, and press Refresh when you want it redrawn.

title: Everything at once
text: The Parameters panel is the same information as a table: every parameter of every fit and every plugin group, filterable, with value, bounds, fixed state and the row it follows. Right-click the header to choose the columns; type a row number into ‘Link row’ to link.

title: Keep the scheme
text: Save writes the network — values, fixed flags and links — as a GraphML file. Loading it applies all three onto the fits you have open, which is how one linking scheme is reused on a new set of datasets.
